name: Helon
title: Father of Eliab from the tribe of Zebulun
summary: Helon is known from the Bible as the father of Eliab, who was the leader and chief of the tribe of Zebulun during the wilderness wanderings. He is mentioned several times in the Book of Numbers in connection with the census and the arrangement of the tribes in the camp and during the march. Although little is known about Helon personally, his significance is tied to his son Eliab's leadership role.

keyEvents.title: Census in the wilderness
keyEvents.description: Helon's son Eliab was appointed as leader of the tribe of Zebulun during the first census in the wilderness of Sinai.

keyEvents.title: Arrangement of the tribes in the camp
keyEvents.description: Eliab, son of Helon, was assigned his place in the camp arrangement with the tribe of Zebulun under Judah's banner on the east side of the tabernacle.

keyEvents.title: Offerings of the chiefs at the altar
keyEvents.description: Eliab, son of Helon, brought his offering as chief of Zebulun at the dedication of the tabernacle, on the third day.

keyEvents.title: Commander of Zebulun's army during the march
keyEvents.description: Eliab, son of Helon, led the army of the tribe of Zebulun when the children of Israel broke camp and marched through the wilderness.
